tests.note: WORDS keeps a,b,c as single job id — same class as prior W2

tests.name: print_json_bag_collapse
tests.note: processed shows as p2p1 — newlines collapsed in JSON string

tests.name: write_append_glue
tests.cmd: SYS WRITE path line1; SYS APPEND path line2
tests.note: file becomes line1line2 — no auto NL between WRITE body and APPEND

weaknesses.title: WRITE body has no trailing NL — APPEND glues next line
weaknesses.detail: SYS WRITE path 'line1' then SYS APPEND path 'line2' yields file bytes 'line1line2\n'. Line-oriented report plates built with WRITE header + APPEND fields silently corrupt the first boundary. Agents must PUSH into a bag then single WRITE, or ensure header ends with \n (no easy in-lang ensure-NL form).

weaknesses.title: PRINT_JSON collapses newlines inside bag strings
weaknesses.detail: PRINT_JSON processed after multi-job FIFO shows 'p2p1' not 'p2\np1'. Agents cannot re-parse multi-line bag fields from JSON dumps; must use scalar counts or plate files.
weaknesses.repro: LET bag='a\nb'; PRINT_JSON bag → "bag":"ab" class collapse

weaknesses.title: WORDS is whitespace-only — comma job lists stay one token
weaknesses.detail: CUBALC_QUEUE_PUSH=a,b,c enqueues one job id 'a,b,c'. Same WORDS edge as mesh fanout; agents need SPLIT ',' first for CSV-style env.
weaknesses.repro: WORDS 'a,b,c' → single field; DONE plate has a,b,c

weaknesses.title: SYS PUSH of a multi-line string expands into multiple fields
weaknesses.detail: SYS PUSH bag 'a\nb' increases field count by 2 (hdr→3 fields). Cannot push a multi-line blob as one opaque field; report 'processed' section becomes flat fields after the key. Agents needing opaque blobs need REPLACEALL of \n or a dedicated escape.

weaknesses.title: WRITE of bag often omits final trailing newline
weaknesses.detail: QUEUE.txt after single remain field is 'jobC' without trailing $. Multi-line bags write internal \n but last field has no final NL. Harmless for CubalC READ/LINES; shell wc -l and some editors undercount.

weaknesses.title: Multi-PREPEND reverses listed priority order
weaknesses.detail: EACH PREPEND p1 then p2 leaves p2 at front (POPHEAD first). Documented intentional for stack-front insert; agents who want list-order priority must REVL the prio list first or PREPEND in reverse.
weaknesses.repro: PRIORITY='p1 p2' → processed p2 then p1

workarounds: Build report bags with SYS PUSH then one SYS WRITE (avoid WRITE+APPEND for multi-field plates)
PRINT_JSON only scalar counters; put multi-line lists on STATE plates
SPLIT ',' before WORDS for CSV job env lists
REVL prio list before EACH PREPEND if list order should match POPHEAD order
APPEND alone for line logs (DONE.txt) — it terminates lines; do not mix bare WRITE without NL
language_gaps: WRITE that always ends plates with trailing newline (or APPEND that separates if missing NL)
PRINT_JSON escape of \n \t in string values
PUSH_FIELD / push with escape so multi-line blobs stay one field
WORDS sep=',' or TOKENIZE with custom delimiter (SPLIT already exists — doc recipe)
Optional FIFO plate form (enqueue/dequeue durable queue without manual WRITE loop)
